news.title: Restoring their smiles
news.author: Dr. Michael Msafiri
news.summary: How a 6-hours visit brought smiles to Penina, Alinda and Neema, who were shy at school.
news.content: Penina, Alinda, and Neema sat quietly in the back row when we visited their center for dental screening, oral health education, and Atraumatic Restorative Treatment (ART). After noticing that their participation in games was almost zero, we invited them to our booth. We taught them how to brush their teeth, clean their tongues, and care for their mouths. Along with the other children, they received toothbrushes and toothpaste. By the end of the event, they burst into big smiles. This was incredibly encouraging, and we hope to see them again soon.

news.title: Critical Link Between Children's Oral Health & Physical Impairement
news.author: Dr. Michael Msafiri
news.summary: Screening for oral health to children with special healthcare needs during the JUST FOR ME charity.
news.content: Every child deserves a healthy smile and a supportive community. During our  JUST FOR ME charity event, our dedicated dental team provided specialized oral health screenings tailored specifically for children with special healthcare needs from different centers. Children with developmental, physical, or sensory challenges often face unique barriers to traditional dental care. Our mission was to break down those barriers. We transformed a routine checkup into a gentle, sensory-friendly experience, ensuring each child felt safe, valued, and comfortable.Our team delivered critical preventative care, including Desensitization practices to reduce dental anxiety, Comprehensive oral screenings to catch hidden decay early, Customized hygiene plans tailored to each child's unique abilities and Caregiver education with practical tips for specialized home care.

news.title: Maintaining Oral Health is a daily uphill battle for children with Cerebral Palsy
news.author: Dr. Sylvia Shilinde
news.summary: We have successfully integrated a unified oral health promotion program to children with Cerebral Palsy and their caregivers.
news.content:
For children with Cerebral Palsy, maintaining oral health is a daily, uphill battle. It is not just about brushing teeth; it is about overcoming complex physical and physiological hurdles that many take for granted: Involuntary biting reflexes and rigid jaw muscles make opening the mouth painful and exhausting, Frequent acid reflux quickly erodes tooth enamel, leaving teeth highly vulnerable to severe, rapid decay, Limited hand and finger dexterity makes gripping a standard toothbrush impossible without help, Poor muscle control increases choking risks, making standard toothpaste and rinsing dangerous.

We addressed these issues and demonstrated better techniques to overcome such challenges.

journey.title: JUST FOR ME CHARITY – MLIMANI CITY
journey.desc: We collaborated with Just For Me Foundation in December 2024 to organize a one-day charity event which gathered 300+ children with physical impairment and orphans from various centers in and around Dar es Salaam. Services provided: dental screening, oral hygiene instructions through demonstrations, oral health education to caregivers on how to handle the oral health status of these children. Products offered: toothbrushes and toothpastes.

journey.title: AT VIGWAZA PWANI - MAASAI COMMUNITY
journey.desc: We collaborated with Kesho Angavu Initiative (KAI) to serve the Masai Community at Vigwaza, a Maasai community in Pwani. This was a 3-days event and we served 150+ children from the Maasai community living in rural areas. We addressed issues pertaining to oral health, screened for dental abnormalities and encouraged proper oral hygiene maintenance.

journey.title: IN SINGISA VILLAGE MOROGORO
journey.desc: We had a trip to Singisa Village, more than 260 KM from Dar es Salaam city center for a dental camp. In this village, there is no internet. A single school and dispensary are found far away from residential spots. This was a one week program. In this village we served 700+ children. We had a dental booth where we did dental screening, oral hygiene instructions, counselling on oral health matters and Atraumatic Restorative Treatments (ART).

journey.title: DORCAS HOMECARE CENTRE
journey.desc: This is a center for children with Cerebral Palsy. These children have uncoordinated motor functions. This tendency makes their muscles stiff sometimes and this makes it hard for their caregivers to clean their oral cavity. So, we visited this center on the WORLD ORAL HEALTH DAY 2025. Services offered: oral health education to caregivers, oral hygiene instructions to caregivers, dental screening of both children and caregivers. Dental Products offered: toothpastes and toothbrushes.

journey.title: AT SIFA VILLAGE ORPHANAGE CENTER
journey.desc: We collaborated with Walimwengu Foundation in paying a visit this center for charity purpose. At this community we managed to serve 100+ orphans and 50+ adults. Services offered: oral health education, oral hygiene instructions, dental screening and counselling on matters pertaining oral health.

journey.title: AT JERUSALEM CHILDREN’S HOME
journey.desc: We collaborated with Agents Of Smile Foundation on 21st March, 2026 at Jerusalem Children’s Home in conducting a charity outreach. At this center we served 60+ who are orphans and others abandoned. We did oral hygiene screening, oral health promotion and gave oral hygiene kits.
